## `EntryDllPath`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.EntryDllPath` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The rules for a manifest's `entryDll`: a relative path inside the pack folder that names the code mod's assembly. Pure string logic, shared by the manifest parser, [`PackManifest`](#packmanifest) and [`PackResolver`](#packresolver), so all three agree on what a valid path is and what it matches.

<a id="entrydllpath--extension"></a>

### `const string Extension = ".dll"`

The file extension an entry assembly must have.

<a id="entrydllpath--islisted"></a>

### `static bool IsListed(IEnumerable<string> files, string entryDll)`

True when a pack's file listing contains the entry assembly. Case-insensitive, because both macOS and Windows file systems are by default, and a manifest that says `mymod.dll` for `MyMod.dll` loads there.

**Parameters**

- `files`: The pack's files, relative to its root, any separator style.
- `entryDll`: A normalised `entryDll`.

<a id="entrydllpath--simplename"></a>

### `static string SimpleName(string path)`

The assembly's simple name as the file names it: `bin/MyMod.dll` gives `MyMod`. The real name lives in the assembly's metadata; this is the name the runtime probes for.

**Parameters**

- `path`: A relative path to a `.dll`.

<a id="entrydllpath--trynormalise"></a>

### `static bool TryNormalise(string raw, out string normalised, out string problem)`

Normalises and validates a raw `entryDll` value.

**Parameters**

- `raw`: The value as written in the manifest.
- `normalised`: The path with forward slashes and no leading `./`, e.g. `MyMod.dll` or `bin/MyMod.dll`; null when invalid.
- `problem`: Why it is invalid, written for the pack author; null when valid.

**Returns:** True when the value is a usable relative path to a `.dll` inside the pack.

<a id="gameversiondifference"></a>

## `GameVersionDifference`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.GameVersionDifference` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

How far apart two game versions are, as [`GameVersions.Difference`](#gameversions--difference-string-string) reports it.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="gameversiondifference--same"></a>`Same` | 0 | The same version. Build metadata (`+…`) and surrounding whitespace are ignored. |
| <a id="gameversiondifference--patch"></a>`Patch` | 1 | Only the patch number differs, e.g. `1.17.2` and `1.17.3`. |
| <a id="gameversiondifference--minor"></a>`Minor` | 2 | The minor number differs, e.g. `1.17.3` and `1.18.0`. |
| <a id="gameversiondifference--major"></a>`Major` | 3 | The major number differs, e.g. `1.17.3` and `2.0.0`. |
| <a id="gameversiondifference--prerelease"></a>`Prerelease` | 4 | Same major.minor.patch, different pre-release tag, e.g. `1.18.0-beta.1` and `1.18.0`. |
| <a id="gameversiondifference--unknown"></a>`Unknown` | 5 | At least one side is missing or is not a version number, and the two texts are not identical, so how far apart they are cannot be said. |

<a id="gameversions"></a>

## `GameVersions`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.GameVersions` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Game version strings, as the running game reports them (`UnityEngine.Application.version`) and as pack manifests declare them: lenient parsing into [`SemVer`](#semver), and comparison.

Shared by the pack policy ([`PackGameVersionCheck`](#packgameversioncheck)) and by the framework's own target-drift explanation (`CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.GameVersionGate`), so both describe a difference in the same words.

<a id="gameversions--unknown"></a>

### `const string Unknown = "unknown"`

Displayed in place of a version the game did not report.

<a id="gameversions--describe"></a>

### `static string Describe(string reference, string actual)`

A short phrase saying how `actual` relates to `reference`: `newer patch version`, `older minor version`, `newer major version` or `older build (pre-release tag differs)`. Null when the two are the same or either is not a version number.

**Parameters**

- `reference`: The version something was made or verified for.
- `actual`: The version actually running.

<a id="gameversions--difference-semver-semver"></a>

### `static GameVersionDifference Difference(SemVer from, SemVer to)`

How far apart two parsed versions are. Build metadata is ignored.

**Parameters**

- `from`: The reference version.
- `to`: The version compared against it.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: Either argument is null.

<a id="gameversions--difference-string-string"></a>

### `static GameVersionDifference Difference(string from, string to)`

How far apart two game versions are. When either side is not a version number the answer is [`GameVersionDifference.Same`](#gameversiondifference--same) for identical (trimmed, ordinal) texts and [`GameVersionDifference.Unknown`](#gameversiondifference--unknown) otherwise.

**Parameters**

- `from`: The reference version, e.g. the one a pack was made for.
- `to`: The version compared against it, e.g. the running game's.

<a id="gameversions--tryparse"></a>

### `static bool TryParse(string text, out SemVer version)`

Parses a game version. SemVer 2.0.0 is tried first; a version of only one or two numeric parts (`1.18`, `2`) is read with the missing parts as zero, because a game is not obliged to print three. Anything else (`1.17.3.1`, `1.17.3b`) fails.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The candidate version; null or blank fails.
- `version`: The parsed version, or null on failure.

**Returns:** True when `text` is a version number.

<a id="packcontentindex"></a>

## `PackContentIndex`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.PackContentIndex` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The classified contents of one pack, built from a plain list of relative file paths.

Path-only by design: it takes a listing, never a directory, so the conventions are unit testable without a filesystem and identical on macOS and Windows. Paths are normalised to forward slashes, de-duplicated case-insensitively (both platforms we ship on have case-insensitive filesystems by default), and ordered ordinally so two scans of the same pack always produce the same index.

The conventions, in the order they are tested:

- **`manifest.json`**: [`PackContentKind.Manifest`](#packcontentkind--manifest)
- **`textures/**.png`**: [`PackContentKind.Texture`](#packcontentkind--texture) (any depth)
- **`audio/voice/*.ogg`, `audio/voice/*.wav`**: [`PackContentKind.Voice`](#packcontentkind--voice)
- **`audio/music/_tracks.json`**: [`PackContentKind.MusicTracks`](#packcontentkind--musictracks)
- **`audio/music/*`**: [`PackContentKind.Music`](#packcontentkind--music)
- **`audio/ambient/*.ogg|wav`**: [`PackContentKind.AmbientAudio`](#packcontentkind--ambientaudio)
- **`audio/ambient_se/*.ogg|wav`**: [`PackContentKind.AmbientSeAudio`](#packcontentkind--ambientseaudio)
- **`audio/se/system/*.ogg|wav`**: [`PackContentKind.SystemSeAudio`](#packcontentkind--systemseaudio)
- **`audio/se/timer/*.ogg|wav`**: [`PackContentKind.TimerSeAudio`](#packcontentkind--timerseaudio)
- **`audio/direction_music/*.ogg|wav`**: [`PackContentKind.DirectionMusicAudio`](#packcontentkind--directionmusicaudio)
- **`data/localization.json`**: [`PackContentKind.Localization`](#packcontentkind--localization)
- **`data/novel.json`**: [`PackContentKind.Novel`](#packcontentkind--novel)
- **`data/scenario_groups.json`**: [`PackContentKind.ScenarioGroups`](#packcontentkind--scenariogroups)
- **`data/triggers.json`**: [`PackContentKind.Triggers`](#packcontentkind--triggers)
- **`data/edit/*.json`**: [`PackContentKind.EditData`](#packcontentkind--editdata) (direct children)
- **`ui/_sprites.json`**: [`PackContentKind.UiSprites`](#packcontentkind--uisprites)
- **`ui/**.png`**: [`PackContentKind.UiSprite`](#packcontentkind--uisprite) (any depth)
- **`language.json`**: [`PackContentKind.Language`](#packcontentkind--language)
- **anything else**: [`PackContentKind.Other`](#packcontentkind--other)

Every match is case-insensitive. A folder convention takes direct children only unless the table says "any depth", so `audio/ambient/old/rain.ogg` is [`PackContentKind.Other`](#packcontentkind--other). An unrecognised file is never an error: packs carry READMEs, source art and notes, and a pack must not fail to load because of them.

### `static PackContentIndex Build(IEnumerable<string> relativePaths)`

Builds an index from a listing of paths relative to the pack root.

<a id="packcontentindex--classify"></a>

### `static PackContentKind Classify(string normalisedPath)`

Classifies one already-normalised relative path. Exposed so a loader can explain why a file it was handed is treated the way it is.

**Parameters**

- `normalisedPath`: A forward-slash relative path, as produced by [`PackContentIndex.Build`](#packcontentindex--build).

<a id="packcontentindex--normalise"></a>

### `static string Normalise(string raw)`

Normalises one listing entry: backslashes become forward slashes and any leading `./` or `/` is dropped. Returns null for an entry that is not a usable relative path: null, blank, one that escapes the pack root with `..`, or one that would mean something else on Windows - a `:` anywhere (`C:/x` and `C:x` are rooted or drive-relative there; `a.txt:s` is a stream), a segment that is a device name (`con`, `nul.png`, `com1.ogg`) or ends in a dot or space ([`SafeFileNames`](#safefilenames)).

**Parameters**

- `raw`: A path as the caller produced it.

<a id="packcontentindex--ofkind"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<PackFile> OfKind(PackContentKind kind)`

Every file of one kind, ordinally ordered by path. Never null.

**Parameters**

- `kind`: The kind to filter by.

<a id="packcontentkind"></a>

## `PackContentKind`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.PackContentKind` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What a file inside a pack is, decided purely from its path by the folder conventions in [`PackContentIndex`](#packcontentindex). The kind says which loader will be asked for the file; it is not a claim that the file's contents are valid.

Members are appended, never renumbered: the value is written into trace records and a reordered enum would make an old trace misleading. The list is frozen; a later feature that needs a convention nobody declared reads its files from [`PackContentKind.Other`](#packcontentkind--other), as the subtitle tables (`data/subtitles/<lang>.json`) already do.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="packcontentkind--other"></a>`Other` | 0 | Anything the conventions do not recognise. Carried, never loaded. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--manifest"></a>`Manifest` | 1 | The pack's own `manifest.json`. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--texture"></a>`Texture` | 2 | A texture under `textures/`. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--voice"></a>`Voice` | 3 | A voice clip under `audio/voice/`. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--music"></a>`Music` | 4 | A music track under `audio/music/` (direct child). The track list `audio/music/_tracks.json` is [`PackContentKind.MusicTracks`](#packcontentkind--musictracks), not a track. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--localization"></a>`Localization` | 5 | `data/localization.json` - dialogue and UI strings. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--novel"></a>`Novel` | 6 | `data/novel.json` - novel/story rows. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--scenariogroups"></a>`ScenarioGroups` | 7 | `data/scenario_groups.json` - scenario group rows. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--language"></a>`Language` | 8 | `language.json` at the pack root - languages the pack declares (`CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Language.LanguageDeclarationParser`). |
| <a id="packcontentkind--editdata"></a>`EditData` | 9 | An EditData file, `data/edit/*.json` (direct children): edits to any master table, Content-Patcher style. Applied in ordinal path order within a pack. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--ambientaudio"></a>`AmbientAudio` | 10 | A replacement clip for an ambient loop, `audio/ambient/*.ogg\|wav`. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--ambientseaudio"></a>`AmbientSeAudio` | 11 | A replacement clip for an ambient one-shot, `audio/ambient_se/*.ogg\|wav`. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--systemseaudio"></a>`SystemSeAudio` | 12 | A replacement clip for a system sound, `audio/se/system/*.ogg\|wav`. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--timerseaudio"></a>`TimerSeAudio` | 13 | A replacement clip for a timer sound, `audio/se/timer/*.ogg\|wav`. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--directionmusicaudio"></a>`DirectionMusicAudio` | 14 | A replacement clip for story ("direction") music, `audio/direction_music/*.ogg\|wav` (the game's `DirectionMusicMaster` table). Reserved in advance so the frozen list does not block it. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--musictracks"></a>`MusicTracks` | 15 | The pack's music track list, `audio/music/_tracks.json`. |
| <a id="packcontentkind--uisprite"></a>`UiSprite` | 16 | A replacement UI sprite, `ui/**.png` at any depth (D-UI). |
| <a id="packcontentkind--uisprites"></a>`UiSprites` | 17 | The UI sprite rules, `ui/_sprites.json` (D-UI). |
| <a id="packcontentkind--triggers"></a>`Triggers` | 18 | The pack's cutscene triggers, `data/triggers.json`. |

## `PackDependency`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.PackDependency` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

One entry of a manifest's `dependsOn` array (or its `contentPackFor`): the pack that must load first, optionally the oldest version of it that will do, and whether the dependency is required at all.

<a id="packdependency--ctor"></a>

### `PackDependency(string id, SemVer minVersion = null, bool optional = false)`

Creates a dependency.

**Parameters**

- `id`: The required pack's id. Required.
- `minVersion`: Oldest acceptable version of that pack, or null for "any version".
- `optional`: True for a soft dependency: when the pack is installed it loads first, and when it is absent or was itself skipped the dependency is ignored. An installed pack older than `minVersion` still refuses the dependent, as a required one would (SMAPI's rule: an optional integration against an old version is a crash waiting to happen).

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `id` is null or blank.

<a id="packdependency--id"></a>

### `string Id { get; }`

The required pack's id.

<a id="packdependency--isoptional"></a>

### `bool IsOptional { get; }`

True for a soft dependency: it orders the load when the pack is present and is ignored when it is not. False (the default) refuses the dependent when the pack is missing.

<a id="packdependency--minversion"></a>

### `SemVer MinVersion { get; }`

Oldest acceptable version, or null when any version satisfies the dependency.

<a id="packdependency--asrequired"></a>

### `PackDependency AsRequired()`

The same dependency with [`PackDependency.IsOptional`](#packdependency--isoptional) false.

<a id="packdependency--issatisfiedby"></a>

### `bool IsSatisfiedBy(SemVer version)`

True when `version` satisfies this dependency.

**Parameters**

- `version`: The version the required pack actually declares.

<a id="packdependency--tostring"></a>

### `override string ToString()`

`id`, `id >= 1.2.0`, with `(optional)` for a soft dependency.

<a id="packgameversioncheck"></a>

## `PackGameVersionCheck`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.PackGameVersionCheck` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The pack game-version policy, SMAPI-like:

- `gameVersion` means "made and tested with". A different running version loads the pack with one warning naming both versions; it is never a reason to skip.
- `minGameVersion` / `maxGameVersion` are optional inclusive bounds compared by SemVer precedence. Outside them the pack is skipped as [`PackSkipReason.GameVersionTooOld`](#packskipreason--gameversiontooold) / [`PackSkipReason.GameVersionTooNew`](#packskipreason--gameversiontoonew), unless game versions are ignored, in which case it loads with a warning.
- A running version that is unknown or not a version number never skips a pack; it warns when the pack declares anything.

Pure and immutable; [`PackResolver`](#packresolver) evaluates it once per pack.

<a id="packgameversioncheck--detail"></a>

One line for the pack author: the skip detail when [`PackGameVersionCheck.Skips`](#packgameversioncheck--skips), the warning when [`PackGameVersionCheck.Warns`](#packgameversioncheck--warns), otherwise what was compared. Never null.

<a id="packgameversioncheck--difference"></a>

How the running game differs from the declared `gameVersion`, or null when the manifest declares no `gameVersion`.

<a id="packgameversioncheck--madefor"></a>

The manifest's `gameVersion`, or null.

<a id="packgameversioncheck--running"></a>

<a id="packgameversioncheck--skips"></a>

True when the pack is skipped.

The text of the one warning line logged when the pack loads, e.g. `made for game 1.17.2, running 1.17.3 (newer patch version); loaded anyway`. Null when there is nothing to warn about, and always null when [`PackGameVersionCheck.Skips`](#packgameversioncheck--skips).

<a id="packgameversionstatus"></a>

## `PackGameVersionStatus`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.PackGameVersionStatus` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What a pack's game-version fields say about the running game.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="packgameversionstatus--notdeclared"></a>`NotDeclared` | 0 | The manifest declares none of `gameVersion`, `minGameVersion`, `maxGameVersion`. Loads silently. |
| <a id="packgameversionstatus--match"></a>`Match` | 1 | The running game is the declared `gameVersion` (or none is declared) and inside the declared range. Loads silently. |
| <a id="packgameversionstatus--differs"></a>`Differs` | 2 | The running game is not the declared `gameVersion` but is inside the declared range. Loads with one warning. |
| <a id="packgameversionstatus--unverified"></a>`Unverified` | 3 | The running game's version is unknown or not a version number, so the declared fields could not be compared. Never a skip: loads with one warning. |
| <a id="packgameversionstatus--tooold"></a>`TooOld` | 4 | The running game is older than `minGameVersion`: skipped as [`PackSkipReason.GameVersionTooOld`](#packskipreason--gameversiontooold), or loaded with a warning when the resolver was told to ignore game versions. |
| <a id="packgameversionstatus--toonew"></a>`TooNew` | 5 | The running game is newer than `maxGameVersion`: skipped as [`PackSkipReason.GameVersionTooNew`](#packskipreason--gameversiontoonew), or loaded with a warning when the resolver was told to ignore game versions. |

<a id="packmanifest"></a>

## `PackManifest`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.PackManifest` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A content pack's or code mod's `manifest.json`, parsed and validated. Immutable; build one with [`PackManifestParser`](#packmanifestparser) rather than by hand outside tests.

The schema (only `id`, `name` and `version` are required):

```csharp
{
  "id": "cwy.example",                  // ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{2,63}$ - unique, stable, lowercase
  "name": "CWY Example Pack",           // shown to humans
  "version": "0.1.0",                   // SemVer 2.0.0
  "author": "you",                      // optional
  "description": "what it does",        // optional
  "gameVersion": "1.17.3",              // optional; "made and tested with" - a different build loads with a warning
  "minGameVersion": "1.17.0",           // optional SemVer; oldest game build it supports (inclusive), else skipped
  "maxGameVersion": "1.17.99",          // optional SemVer; newest game build it supports (inclusive), else skipped
  "loaderVersion": "0.9.0",     // optional; oldest CWY:LS Mod Loader (API version) that can load it
  "entryDll": "MyMod.dll",              // optional; makes this a code mod
  "contentPackFor": "some.codemod",     // optional; this pack is data for that code mod (a required dependency)
  "dependsOn": [                        // optional
    { "id": "other.pack", "minVersion": "1.2.0" },
    { "id": "nice.to.have", "optional": true },
    "another.pack"                      // shorthand for { "id": "another.pack" }
  ]
}
```

<a id="packmanifest--ctor"></a>

### `PackManifest(string id, string name, SemVer version, string author = null, string description = null, string gameVersion = null, SemVer loaderVersion = null, IReadOnlyList<PackDependency> dependsOn = null, SemVer minGameVersion = null, SemVer maxGameVersion = null, string entryDll = null, PackDependency contentPackFor = null, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object> extensions = null)`

Creates a manifest. Validates `id` against [`PackManifest.IdPattern`](#packmanifest--idpattern).

**Parameters**

- `id`: Unique pack id.
- `name`: Human-readable name.
- `version`: The pack's own version.
- `author`: Author, or null.
- `description`: One-line description, or null.
- `gameVersion`: Game build this pack was made and tested with, or null for "not stated".
- `loaderVersion`: Oldest framework version that can load it, or null for "any".
- `dependsOn`: Packs that must load first, or null for none.
- `minGameVersion`: Oldest game build it supports (inclusive), or null for no lower bound.
- `maxGameVersion`: Newest game build it supports (inclusive), or null for no upper bound.
- `entryDll`: Relative path of the code mod's assembly inside the pack folder, or null for a content pack. Normalised with [`EntryDllPath.TryNormalise`](#entrydllpath--trynormalise).
- `contentPackFor`: The code mod this pack is data for, or null. Must be required (not optional), must not be the pack itself, and cannot be combined with `entryDll`.
- `extensions`: The manifest's `x-` members, or null for none.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `id` is malformed, `name` is blank, `minGameVersion` is above `maxGameVersion`, `entryDll` is not a usable path, or `contentPackFor` breaks one of its rules.
- `ArgumentNullException`: `version` is null.

The pattern every pack id must match, as a human-readable string.

<a id="packresolver"></a>

## `PackResolver`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.PackResolver` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Decides which discovered packs and code mods load, in which order, and reports every refusal with a reason. Pure logic over [`IPackSource`](#ipacksource): no filesystem, no Unity, no logging - which is what lets the whole policy be unit-tested. Content packs and code mods (manifests with `entryDll`) share this one dependency graph.

The gates are applied in this order, and the first one that refuses wins:

1. manifest present, then valid
2. id not already claimed by an earlier folder
3. the running game is inside the declared `minGameVersion`/`maxGameVersion` range ([`PackGameVersionCheck`](#packgameversioncheck)); a different `gameVersion` alone is not a gate - the pack loads and [`PackResolution.Warnings`](#packresolution--warnings) carries one line for it
4. declared `loaderVersion` is not newer than this framework
5. a code mod's `entryDll` is in its folder ([`PackSkipReason.EntryDllMissing`](#packskipreason--entrydllmissing))
6. every required dependency (`dependsOn` without `optional`, and `contentPackFor`, which must name a code mod) survived, at a new enough version; an optional dependency that is absent or skipped is ignored, one that is present but too old refuses the dependent
7. the dependency graph is acyclic

A dependency skipped by an earlier gate takes its dependents down with it - reported as [`PackSkipReason.MissingDependency`](#packskipreason--missingdependency) naming the reason the dependency went, so one broken pack does not produce a wall of unexplained skips.

<a id="packresolver--resolve"></a>

### `static PackResolution Resolve(IEnumerable<IPackSource> sources, string currentGameVersion, SemVer coreVersion, bool ignoreGameVersion = false)`

Resolves discovered packs into a load order.

**Parameters**

- `sources`: The candidates, in discovery order. Null entries are ignored; the order is preserved for packs that do not depend on each other, so the log is stable between runs.
- `currentGameVersion`: The running game's version (`UnityEngine.Application.version`), or null when it could not be read. An unknown or unparseable version never skips a pack; a pack that declares a game version then loads with a warning.
- `coreVersion`: This framework's API version (`CwyApi.Version`), compared against each manifest's `loaderVersion`. Null means "unknown", which refuses any pack that declares a minimum.
- `ignoreGameVersion`: True to load packs even when the running game is outside their `minGameVersion`/`maxGameVersion` range (they warn instead), for testing a pack on a game build it does not claim to support.

<a id="packskipreason"></a>

## `PackSkipReason`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.PackSkipReason` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Why [`PackResolver`](#packresolver) refused to load a pack. Every skip is reported with one of these plus a detail string; a pack is never dropped silently.

Values are numbered explicitly so they stay stable if a member is ever retired.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="packskipreason--missingmanifest"></a>`MissingManifest` | 0 | The folder has no readable `manifest.json`. |
| <a id="packskipreason--invalidmanifest"></a>`InvalidManifest` | 1 | The manifest is not valid JSON, or fails the schema. Detail says which member. |
| <a id="packskipreason--duplicateid"></a>`DuplicateId` | 2 | Another folder already claimed this pack id. The first one wins. |
| <a id="packskipreason--coreversiontooold"></a>`CoreVersionTooOld` | 4 | The pack needs a newer CwyLs.ModLoader than the one running. |
| <a id="packskipreason--missingdependency"></a>`MissingDependency` | 5 | A required pack named in `dependsOn` or `contentPackFor` is absent - either never present, or itself skipped - or `contentPackFor` names a pack that is not a code mod. Optional dependencies never produce this. |
| <a id="packskipreason--dependencyversiontoolow"></a>`DependencyVersionTooLow` | 6 | A dependency is present but older than the `minVersion` asked for. |
| <a id="packskipreason--dependencycycle"></a>`DependencyCycle` | 7 | The pack is part of a `dependsOn` cycle, so no load order exists. |
| <a id="packskipreason--gameversiontooold"></a>`GameVersionTooOld` | 8 | The running game is older than the manifest's `minGameVersion`, and the framework was not told to ignore game versions. |
| <a id="packskipreason--gameversiontoonew"></a>`GameVersionTooNew` | 9 | The running game is newer than the manifest's `maxGameVersion`, and the framework was not told to ignore game versions. |
| <a id="packskipreason--entrydllmissing"></a>`EntryDllMissing` | 10 | The manifest names an `entryDll` (a code mod) but that file is not in the pack folder. The whole pack is skipped - its content too - because a code mod's content is usually written for its code. Dependents go with it as [`PackSkipReason.MissingDependency`](#packskipreason--missingdependency). |

## `SafeFileNames`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.SafeFileNames` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

File-name rules that keep a name meaning the same file on macOS and Windows. Pure, so they are unit-tested; used by [`PackContentIndex.Normalise`](#packcontentindex--normalise) for pack paths and by the mod Data facet for data keys.

Windows opens a device, not a file, for `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`-`COM9` and `LPT1`-`LPT9`, with or without an extension and in any case, and it silently drops a trailing dot or space (so `a.txt.` is `a.txt`). A colon makes a path drive-relative (`C:x`) or names an alternate data stream.

<a id="semver"></a>

## `SemVer`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.SemVer` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

Implements: `IComparable<SemVer>`, `IEquatable<SemVer>`

A Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version: `major.minor.patch[-prerelease][+build]`.

Written out rather than taken from a NuGet package because every plugin assembly must load on Unity's Mono profile with no dependencies beyond the game's own, and because the comparison rules - not the parsing - are what pack dependency resolution hangs on.

Ordering follows the spec: numeric comparison of major, minor and patch; a pre-release version is *lower* than the release it precedes (`1.0.0-rc.1 < 1.0.0`); pre-release identifiers compare numerically when all-digits and by ordinal ASCII otherwise, with a numeric identifier always lower than an alphanumeric one; build metadata is ignored in comparison but preserved in [`SemVer.ToString`](#semver--tostring).

<a id="semver--build"></a>

### `string Build { get; }`

Build metadata without the leading `+`, or null. Ignored when comparing.

### `static int Compare(SemVer left, SemVer right)`

Orders two versions, treating null as lower than any version. Build metadata is ignored.

**Parameters**

- `left`: First version, or null.
- `right`: Second version, or null.

### `static bool TryParse(string text, out SemVer version)`

Parses a version, reporting failure instead of throwing.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The candidate version; null or blank fails.
- `version`: The parsed version, or null on failure.

**Returns:** True when `text` is a SemVer 2.0.0 version.

<a id="semver--tryparse-string-ref-semver-ref-string"></a>

### `static bool TryParse(string text, out SemVer version, out string error)`

Parses a version, reporting why it failed.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The candidate version; null or blank fails.
- `version`: The parsed version, or null on failure.
- `error`: Why it failed, or null on success.

**Returns:** True when `text` is a SemVer 2.0.0 version.

## `SkippedPack`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.SkippedPack` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One pack that was found but not loaded, and why.

<a id="skippedpack--ctor"></a>

### `SkippedPack(string id, string folderName, PackSkipReason reason, string detail)`

Creates a skip record.

**Parameters**

- `id`: The pack's id, or its folder name when the manifest never parsed.
- `folderName`: The folder the pack was found in.
- `reason`: Which rule refused it.
- `detail`: The specifics - the invalid member, the missing dependency, ...

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `id` is null or blank.
